name: fork
description: fork() creates a new process by duplicating the calling process. The new process, referred to as the child, is an exact duplicate except for specific attributes like process ID and parent ID, and both run in separate memory spaces.

return_value.success: Returns the PID of the child process in the parent and 0 in the child
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, no child process is created, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: A system-imposed limit on the number of threads was encountered, such as RLIMIT_NPROC, kernel threads-max, or PID limits.
The caller is operating under the SCHED_DEADLINE scheduling policy without the reset-on-fork flag set.
fork() failed to allocate necessary kernel structures due to memory constraints.
An attempt was made to create a child process in a PID namespace whose 'init' process has terminated.
fork() is not supported on this platform, such as hardware without a Memory-Management Unit.
System call was interrupted by a signal and will be restarted.

versions: Since glibc 2.3.3, glibc uses clone(2) instead of the kernel's fork() system call; POSIX.1-2001, SVr4, 4.3BSD.
